head: WhatsApp cloud backup on Android in testing: 2 GB free storage
dek: WhatsApp is testing its own cloud backup on Android, so chats can be backed up on WhatsApp's servers instead of Google Drive, with 2 GB free. It's in beta version 2.26.46.4 for some testers, spotted by WABetaInfo; WhatsApp hasn't said when everyone gets it.
details: The backup screen shows two choices, WhatsApp cloud storage and Google storage, and you can switch at any time. End-to-end encryption is required for backups on WhatsApp's servers, with a passkey or a 64-digit key. More space comes with WhatsApp Plus (100 GB, $2.99 a month, according to 9to5Google) or Meta One (up to 4 TB). After a subscription ends, the latest backup is kept for 4 months, then deleted if you don't renew.
where: Android, WhatsApp beta 2.26.46.4, some testers; more over the coming weeks
means: If your Google Drive is nearly full or you have no Google account, WhatsApp's own backup could give you a second place for your chats once it reaches you.
todo: Nothing to do yet. When it shows up in your chat backup settings, set up the passkey or write down the 64-digit key before the first backup, or you can't restore it.
